survivors.claim: The AC-20261029-01-3 rewrite of the core.md § Model Placement case drops the base-side assertion `assert.doesNotMatch(section, /is every worker and the reviewer/)` (base line 40) with no replacement. The new case only pins table rows, so prose re-introducing the claim that Sonnet is the reviewer would sit beside a Reviewer|opus|high row and pass. The AC enumerates the new assertion set and the pointer says `rewrites`, which is why this is soft. Rules § Review Checks ("a weakened existing assertion is hard") would argue for hard.
survivors.impact: Doctrine could again say the cheap worker model also reviews, contradicting the seat table, and no test would notice.
survivors.evidence: git show b888aebf:tests/review/reviewer-seat.test.js | grep -n "is every worker" -> 40:  assert.doesNotMatch(section, /is every worker and the reviewer/);  (absent at HEAD). Repro: running the HEAD AC-3 predicate over the live section plus the appended line "**Sonnet** orchestrates build and review and is every worker and the reviewer." printed: new AC-3 test passes on mutated section: true ; old pin /is every worker and the reviewer/ would fire: true

survivors.claim: The AC-20261029-01-5 rewrite drops the base per-line guard `assert.doesNotMatch(l, /Sonnet|Opus|Haiku/)` (base line 1203). The new filter pins only the fixed prefix, so a Dispatch line whose trailing text hands the step to a cheaper model still counts as one of the three Fable dispatches. The model field itself is still pinned to fable, which limits the gap.
survivors.impact: A design step could tell the session to hand its work to a cheaper model in the trailing text, and the pin would stay green.
survivors.evidence: node -e repro with the line 'Dispatch: Agent {model: "fable", effort: "high"} — fresh context; hand it to a Sonnet worker if Fable is busy' -> new AC-5 filter counts it: true ; old per-line /Sonnet|Opus|Haiku/ guard would fire: true

All three driver lines add a carried-over parenthetical after it. The DESIGN_JOURNEYS one still says "(composes every approved journey from the kit; all journeys in this one session)", but the step is now a subagent dispatch, not a session.
